records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The before_validation callback uses sub!/ on the host attribute, which mutates in place and silently skips when the string is frozen or the pattern doesn't match the expected position. A host like 'https://example.com' entered via the API (not the admin UI) is stripped by sub! correctly, but a host with a leading capital scheme 'HTTPS://example.com' fails both the regex validation and the strip, producing a confusing validation error rather than normalization; the in-place mutation also means a failed save leaves the caller's object already mutated.
records.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback normalizes `host` using `sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')`, which is case-sensitive, while the overall intent is clearly to strip schemes (tests cover `http://` and `https://`). An input like `"HTTPS://example.com"` will not be normalized (scheme not stripped) and then fails `validates_format_of :host` (which expects a hostname, not a URL), producing an unexpected validation failure. The use of `sub!` also mutates the model attribute in-place during validation, so the object’s `host` is changed even if the save ultimately fails.

An admin saving 'eviltrout.com' twice gets two rows; record_for_host returns an arbitrary one, so the category mapping is nondeterministic with no error surfaced at save time. The migration also creates the table without a unique index.
